reviewBoundary: Three new complete 15-gap senior cloze narratives, each with four manually written alternatives. Same-author context review covers the correct key and all distractors; structural Gaokao alignment is not a claim of past-paper status or calibrated difficulty.

units.title: 完形填空 · 墙上的球衣

materials.title: The shirt on the wall
materials.text:
Before our football final, I asked Dad for a new shirt. Mine had a torn shoulder and a faded number. He offered to ____1____ it first.

I was disappointed, but went with him to buy thread. Behind the sports-shop counter hung an even more ____2____ shirt, with torn sleeves and a muddy mark. Yet it was displayed in a ____3____, protected by glass.

"My daughter wore that when her team won their first cup," the shopkeeper explained. The mark came from a fall just before she scored.

"Why didn't she wash it?" I asked.

"She did," the woman said, ____4____. "Some marks stay. We decided this one could stay on the wall too."

At home, I examined my own shirt. Its tear came from stretching to stop a ball. I had forgotten that ____5____ until I saw the broken threads. The shirt was a ____6____ of games I had played.

Dad showed me how to hold the cloth while his stitches pulled the edges ____7____. The repair was visible, but strong.

At the final, a teammate noticed it. Instead of trying to ____8____ the stitches, I told their story. He showed me a patch on his shorts. We laughed about where our clothes had been ____9____.

We lost by one goal. I was too disappointed to speak. Dad waited, then asked whether I wanted to ____10____ the shirt. I shook my head. It held the final too, although that memory was not a ____11____ one.

I still like new things. But wearing that shirt, I see more than ____12____ cloth. I remember the field, Dad's hands and a team that played until the ____13____ whistle. The stitches did not make us win. They helped me ____14____ something I had wanted to discard. Some things become more ____15____ because we have used them, not less.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A tear prompts repair, later done with stitches. Weighing does not mend it, delivery is not requested, and borrowing the narrator's existing shirt does not address the damage.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Torn sleeves and a dark mark support damaged. No price, comfort test or popularity comparison supports the other adjectives.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A shirt hanging on the wall protected by glass is in a frame. Basket, pocket and suitcase do not match that display.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The warm explanation of a treasured shirt fits smiling. The speaker remains present and neither disputes an opponent nor shows any cue for sneezing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The tear recalls the moment of stretching for the ball. Price, address and size are not the event just described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The shirt reminds the narrator of past games. It does not predict future games, state rules or constitute a prize awarded for them.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Stitching joins the two torn edges together. Outside, upstairs and backwards do not express the repair's joining action.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Rather than concealing the visible stitches, the narrator explains them. Counting, copying and improving are not the contrast established by sharing their story.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The stitches and patch are mended areas. Neither garment is being sold, designed from scratch or packed in the exchange.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Dad asks whether to discard the shirt after the defeat; the narrator shakes his head and keeps it. Exchange, advertise and rent introduce transactions rather than this keep-or-discard choice.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Losing the final makes this memory not happy. It is recent rather than distant, not secret, and no false recollection is suggested.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Worn cloth describes the old damaged shirt. Material is not established as silk; it is used and visible, excluding unused and invisible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Kept playing until the final whistle expresses persistence through the end. First would stop at the opening, while missing and silent have no support.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The change is learning to value a formerly disposable object. Replace conflicts with retaining it; lending and measuring do not capture its remembered significance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Memories make used objects meaningful. Formality, identity and fashion are not the quality developed through personal experience in this passage.

units.title: 完形填空 · 第一张木刻印画

materials.title: The first print
materials.text:
At a woodcut workshop, I drew a boat on a wooden block: a black sail, pale waves and a bird. The instructor explained that the parts we cut away would remain ____1____ on the paper. Impatient to start, I nodded.

After cutting, I rolled ink onto the block and pressed paper against it. The boat faced the ____2____ direction, and its name appeared backwards.

"I've ruined it," I said.

"You've discovered something about the ____3____," the instructor replied. "Can you use it?"

I wanted an eraser, but the removed wood could not simply be ____4____. I had to use the block as it was.

The reversed boat seemed to be leaving the harbour instead of returning. That gave me an ____5____: a picture about departure. The backwards name was unreadable, so I cut it away, creating a patch that would be ____6____ by the paper's colour.

I printed again, using blue paper. The empty patch became blue, while the inked boat stayed black. This unplanned combination created a feeling I ____7____, like looking across water before sunrise.

Not every accidental cut was useful. One line through the bird bothered me. The instructor helped me ____8____ surrounding marks until the line became part of a cloud. It took care, rather than simply declaring a mistake beautiful.

I kept both prints. The first recorded my ____9____; the second showed my response to them.

Now I study instructions and make small tests first. Yet a result need not match my first drawing to be ____10____. A material may suggest a direction I had not ____11____. I can follow it without pretending I ____12____ it all along.

The boat on my wall remains a ____13____ of that afternoon. I stopped seeking an impossible eraser and began ____14____ to what the block could do. The plan changed, but the work ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Cut-away recesses receive no surface ink and remain unprinted, later taking the paper's colour. Heavy is not a printing state; raised reverses removal; wet is not the lasting result described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A reversed print faces the opposite direction, with backwards text. Safest has no navigation criterion, usual no established habit, and correct contradicts the initial unwanted reversal.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Reversal and cut-away printing are properties of the process. No customer or weather is involved, and the harbour is pictured content rather than the technique discovered.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Removed wood cannot simply be replaced like erasing a pencil mark. Weighed, delivered and named do not restore the missing material.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The new interpretation suggests an idea for a departure image. It is not an appointment, an excuse to stop or an instruction ordered by someone else.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The unprinted patch is visually filled by the paper's colour. Hidden would conceal it rather than make the colour visible; weighed and torn do not describe colour occupying a space.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The narrator adopts the combination and warmly associates it with water before sunrise, supporting liked. Feared, forgot and doubted conflict with recognising and using this welcome effect.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Changing surrounding marks integrates the line into a cloud: adjust. Selling or counting does not alter the image; ignoring contradicts the careful change described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The first print records misunderstanding the process, contrasted with the response after recognition. There are no earnings, actual journeys or promises recorded by it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: A changed outcome can still be worthwhile. Identical to the first plan would contradict change; predictability is not the value discovered; unfinished would not be an achievement sought.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The material reveals an unconsidered creative direction. It is not prohibited, repeated from an earlier attempt or bought.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The narrator honestly distinguishes adaptation from having planned the result all along. Delivered, lost and measured do not express falsely claiming original intention.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The displayed boat recalls the afternoon: a reminder. It is not a navigational map, forecast or purchase receipt.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Working with actual material is responding to its properties. Objecting resists them, apologising is unrelated, and returning to what it can do does not fit the first discovery and change described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Despite the changed plan, the work continued into a second successful print. Vanished, stopped and failed contradict the completed adopted picture.

units.title: 完形填空 · 漫画里的声音

materials.title: A sound on the page
materials.text:
Translating my first comic seemed straightforward until I reached a panel without dialogue. Enormous letters represented a door closing. I typed the dictionary equivalent beneath it. The meaning was ____1____, but a reader had to stop watching the action to ____2____ my note.

The artist pointed at the original lettering. Its rough edges and sharp angle followed the door's movement, almost touching a frightened character. The letters were part of the ____3____, not merely replaceable words.

I drew a shorter sound word into the panel. My neat, rounded letters fitted, but made the door seem ____4____. "That sounds like putting a cup on a table," the artist laughed.

In the scene, wind slammed the door and made the character jump. The lettering needed to preserve that ____5____. Vocabulary alone was not ____6____.

After several attempts, I produced uneven letters stretching across the space. The artist recognised the effect. We checked that they did not ____7____ the face or interfere with the next speech bubble. A change to one part still had to work with the whole page.

Translation now seemed both wider and more ____8____. A dictionary could not settle every decision, but I had more tools than expected. Size, position and shape could carry an effect that a note would only ____9____.

I showed the draft to a friend unfamiliar with the original. She followed the action easily. Her response was not proof for every reader, but a useful ____10____.

The final page omitted my explanatory sentence. I did not regret its ____11____. It had clarified the meaning, then outlived its role. Sometimes a draft matters because of what it enables you to ____12____.

I kept the early versions as a record of the ____13____ leading to a better decision. Now I ask not only what a mark means, but how it asks a reader to ____14____. That question has made me a more ____15____ translator.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The dictionary equivalent gets the meaning accurate but fails as a visual effect. Secret and forgotten conflict with the explicit note; irrelevant contradicts its correct semantic relation to the sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A reader must read the explanatory note, interrupting attention to the action. Drawing, hiding and signing it are not the audience's use of a printed note.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Position, shape and movement make the letters part of the image. Contract, schedule and dictionary are not the visual panel containing them.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Rounded neat lettering softens the effect, confirmed by the quiet cup-on-table comparison. Dangerous reverses that comparison; invisible is impossible for a drawn door; distant lacks a spatial cue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The sudden noise makes the character jump, so shock. Silence contradicts the noise, while agreement and permission are not reactions described in the scene.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary alone is insufficient because lettering must carry the effect too. Legality, popularity and cost are not the limitation being investigated.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: They check that enlarged letters do not obscure the face or impede following dialogue. Imitate, recognise and describe do not express visual blocking.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: More dimensions require judgments beyond a dictionary, making translation demanding. Automatic and uniform deny those choices; temporary concerns duration rather than complexity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Visual tools carry an effect directly while a note explains it. Prevent, purchase and forget do not describe what an explanatory note does.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: One reader's response is a useful indication, expressly not proof for all readers. Guarantee overstates evidence; payment and excuse do not refer to a comprehension response.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The explanatory sentence is absent from the final page, so its removal. Publication and arrival contradict absence; its accuracy was not regretted or rejected.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A draft helps identify and change weak decisions. Charge, promise and own do not capture the revision process described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Repeated lettering trials are experiments leading to the decision. No customers, permission requests or travel destinations are recorded.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The writer considers the response a visual mark invites, such as shock. Compete and pay are unrelated; readers are not being asked to translate the comic themselves.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Careful attention to visual function makes an attentive translator. Fame and wealth have no evidence, and hurried contradicts the repeated thoughtful trials.
